title: test-0109-SOC-HIS-MAURYA
passage: Q: Who founded the Mauryan Empire? A: Chandragupta Maurya established the empire with the guidance of his wise advisor, Chanakya. Chanakya was a brilliant teacher, not a king. Q: What was the Kalinga War? A: Kalinga was a powerful coastal kingdom. Ashoka fought a long, difficult war to conquer it. The massive loss of life made him feel deep regret, leading him to abandon violence. Q: What was Ashoka’s Dhamma? A: Dhamma was a set of moral principles focused on kindness, respect for elders, and tolerance. Ashoka did not force people to follow Buddhism or any specific religion; he simply wanted his subjects to live in peace and harmony. Q: How did Ashoka spread his message? A: Ashoka had his instructions carved onto polished stone pillars and large rock surfaces. These inscriptions were permanent records for his people to read, as paper was not used for official government announcements during that time. Q: Where was the capital located? A: The heart of the administration was Pataliputra, a grand city that served as the capital of the vast empire.
summary: Ashoka fought a long, hard war to conquer it. What was Ashoka’s Dhamma? Ashoka didn't make people follow any religion, he just wanted them to live together in peace and harmony.
